tour.title: The current boot menu
tour.caption: Historical 5 November VM capture of the retained old development ISO. Kubuntu labels remain; this image predates owner hardening and must not be installed. A final OREZ boot menu is still required.
tour.kind: Historical VM — not a new boot test

tour.title: Installation is currently blocked
tour.caption: The actual live-media guard displays why installation is unavailable and exits 78. No installer or disk write was performed.

tour.title: Welcome home: login theme
tour.caption: Actual SDDM theme test mode. The environment has no usable desktop session, so sign-in is unavailable. This is not a successful boot or authentication test.

tour.title: Password field
tour.caption: Dummy text is masked in the real login field. The completed installer must create your local owner password; no Google or Microsoft login is required.

tour.title: Current welcome document
tour.caption: The shipped local help document rendered in host Chromium from its source, at desktop and phone widths. Native Brave/file-URL launch is not tested by this render. A first-run setup wizard remains planned.

tour.title: Your desktop
tour.caption: Actual nested Plasma desktop with the approved Rest wallpaper. The test account retains its demo palette. KDE taskbar/icons are still visible; this is not the final polished shell or a booted ISO.

tour.title: Find OREZ applications
tour.caption: Actual launcher search shows Store, Connect, Settings, Calendar, hardware tools and Welcome. Android entries exist but their consumer runtime remains deferred.

tour.title: Searchable Settings
tour.caption: Typed Bluetooth into native Settings; matching results appeared. Clearing the query and closing Settings also passed.

tour.title: Network settings
tour.caption: Native NetworkManager settings open and close. This offline container has no physical Wi-Fi radio; no connection or hotspot claim.

tour.title: Wi-Fi password controls
tour.caption: A dummy wireless credential was masked, revealed, remasked, cleared and cancelled. No connection was saved. This does not test actual Wi-Fi authentication.

tour.title: Bluetooth settings
tour.caption: The actual page correctly reports no Bluetooth adapter in the container. Target-PC pairing, audio and file transfer are pending.

tour.title: Phone connection
tour.caption: Real KDE Connect window, no paired phone. KDE Connect handles transfers/control; scrcpy provides separate consented screen mirroring. No Realme mirroring session was fabricated.

tour.title: File operations
tour.caption: A disposable text file was copied, renamed, moved to Trash and restored with Undo through the real Dolphin UI. The original and restored bytes matched. No user data or physical drive was touched.

tour.title: Tabs and split view
tour.caption: Real Dolphin tabs and two panes, showing the restored renamed file. Split/tabs visually confirmed; nested function-key automation was replaced with actual menu/button input.

tour.title: OREZ Store
tour.caption: The native Store detects installed Brave, VLC and SuperTux. VLC launched from its button. Android app entries are explicitly pending, not functional Play Store downloads.

tour.title: OREZ Calendar
tour.caption: Actual local event creation/editing, SQLite persistence, ICS export and cancellable deletion passed. No cloud account or remote request.

tour.title: Reuz clock
tour.caption: Native timezone and 12/24-hour preferences saved without changing the system clock. This is the current OREZ Reuz component, not a claim about another repository release.

tour.title: Reuz countdown
tour.caption: Start, pause, resume and completion passed. It is an application timer; suspended-PC wake and physical alarm audio are not verified.

tour.title: Reuz stopwatch
tour.caption: Start/pause, lap and reset passed. Closing active work asks for confirmation and cancellation keeps the app open.

tour.title: OREZ Ink palette
tour.caption: Real Reuz rendering with the packaged Ink palette. Both Paper and Ink were applied; the five proposed future themes are not implemented.

tour.title: Horizon wallpaper
tour.caption: Your second supplied wallpaper applied in the real desktop, then restored to Rest. A wallpaper change is not a new OS edition.

tour.title: Fullscreen VLC
tour.caption: Generated local video played. Actual Space pause/resume, mouse menu, F fullscreen on/off and Ctrl+Q passed. GPU decoding, physical audio and streaming were not tested.

tour.title: Fullscreen native game
tour.caption: SuperTux rendered at 1440×900. Captures show the player moving from x≈96 to x≈482 after Right input. This is software rendering, not an RTX benchmark, Android emulation or universal game compatibility.

tour.title: Game pause menu
tour.caption: Escape opened the actual game pause menu. Only the disposable native game session was stopped.

tour.title: Files and terminal together
tour.caption: Dolphin and Konsole arranged side by side. Minimize and restore also passed. Ordinary user UID 1500, not a privileged desktop session.

tour.title: A second workspace
tour.caption: KWin created a second workspace, switched to it, returned and removed the test workspace. The windows stayed on their original workspace.

tour.title: Restart the panel, preserve the work
tour.caption: A controlled Plasma shell restart brought the panel back while the existing Dolphin/Konsole processes remained alive. This is not kernel-crash, power-loss or disk-recovery qualification.

tour.title: Brave: honest environment limit
tour.caption: The official native Linux browser was attempted. Its sandbox could not create required nested namespaces. This report records BLOCKED, even though the vendor wrapper returned zero; no working browser or YouTube is claimed.
tour.kind: Test report — not a browser window

tour.title: AI status is visible
tour.caption: orezctl ai explicitly reports NOT ENABLED. No AI/MCP root or remote action broker is installed. Future AI must use ordinary permissions and explicit owner approval.

latest_owner_direction: Native Linux Brave; YouTube optional; consented scrcpy mirroring prioritized, not yet tested with a phone. Local account created during setup, no existing online account required.
